newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil - barge premiums ease, cargoes hold.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil - barge premiums ease, cargoes hold.

text.p: NWE gas oil ended mixed on Wednesday with heating oil barge premiums weakening, but other premiums retaining strength or actually firming.
April IPE last traded unchanged at $165.50 a tonne in very thin volume.
Heating oil barges lost ground amid poor interest with trades concluded at April IPE +25 cents fob ARA, off 50 cents.

Offers on Russian cargoes were steady around April IPE +$2 cif against bids which were as low as April flat. Traders said interest in Russian fob was still strong on the back of the arbitrage to Asia although some market players were becoming cautious about how long the window east would remain open.
"Some people want to load cargoes by April 10-15 while others seem happy loading late April," said one dealer.
A lack of suitable freight to shift material eastwards was the major problem, traders said.

Diesel cargo premiums showed some renewed strength with a trade done at April IPE +$11 cif NWE. Late afternoon talk was pegging the market around May IPE +$10 cif on the bid side and May IPE +$12.50 on the offer. Traders said it was a lack of supplies which had pushed prices higher.
FOD was little discussed with the market reasonably balanced between tight supplies and limited demand.
"There's a bit of interest for 5kt, 10kt towards the end of the month," said one trader.
